font.title: Font
font.description: Choose the font you enjoy reading most. All of them are free and open source — nobody will send you (or me) a bill later. Your selection is saved on this device. In languages with non-Latin scripts (Hindi, Bengali, Korean, Punjabi), Noto Sans takes over automatically.

system.note: The font your device already comes with. Nothing extra loads — though it looks slightly different on every computer, which most people never notice.

sourceSans3.note: Calm, friendly, holds up even in long texts. The solid default choice: you rarely stand out with it, which is usually the goal.

inter.note: Clear, modern, everywhere. If the internet feels familiar, there's a decent chance this font is why.

ibmPlexSans.note: A bit more technical in character, with particularly distinct numbers and letters. Serious, calm, never loud — the font that says nothing in meetings yet catches everything.

bricolageGrotesque.note: Has a strong opinion about how letters should look. Interesting to read — if you like fonts that push back a little.

atkinsonHyperlegible.note: Designed so letters can no longer be confused with one another. Helpful for limited vision or when reading is otherwise tiring. Works only in Latin script though — for Hindi, Bengali, Korean, and Punjabi there is no comparably accessible font yet; Noto Sans takes over there.

andika.note: Originally made for first-time readers: large, clearly distinguishable letters with plenty of space between them. Reduces reading effort — helpful for concentration difficulties, declining eyesight, or simply at the end of a long day.

lexend.note: Looks almost normal but helps subtly: scientifically proven faster reading speed. A font that quietly gets its work done — which is what fonts should do.

openDyslexic.note: Developed specifically for people with dyslexia. Letters have a distinct weight at the bottom so b and d, p and q no longer get mixed up. Looks unusual at first glance — and for those affected, that is often exactly why it is a real relief.

playground.description: What happens when the developer has an idea at 1 AM. Stays in because it gives the proof of concept some extra scope — and because vibe coding sometimes crashes into a wall and cool things emerge.
playground.cursorTrailDescription: Leaves a glowing trail behind your cursor. Looks cool. Does nothing productive — much like a daily standup that takes 45 minutes.
playground.cursorTrailPreview: Move your mouse over this. Doesn't it look nice? No? Whatever, I think it looks nice.

privacy.dataControlDetail: You have full control over your data. You can disable progress tracking, export your data, or completely reset everything at any time.
privacy.dataInfoDescription: Learn more about what data is stored and how.
privacy.dataTransmissionDetail: Your learning progress is stored exclusively locally and never transmitted to servers. If you allow usage statistics, anonymized data (page views, time spent, device information) is sent to our own server — never to third parties.

dataType.quizProgress: Completed quizzes, checkpoints, and learning paths (only with your consent)

privacy.description: Control how your learning progress is stored and managed.
privacy.progressDescription: Save which quizzes, checkpoints, and learning paths you have completed, locally in your browser. Off until you switch it on; it is the same choice as in the cookie banner.
privacy.storageLocationDetail: Your learning progress (completed quizzes, checkpoints, and learning paths) is stored in your browser's localStorage only after you agree, and it does not leave your device. If you additionally allow usage statistics, anonymized usage data is sent to our own server (see cookie settings).
privacy.title: Privacy & Progress
privacy.trackingDisabledDetail: All existing progress has been deleted and new progress will not be stored.
privacy.trackingEnabledDetail: Your completed quizzes, checkpoints, and learning paths are now saved locally, including what you did earlier in this visit.
privacy.cookieSettingsDescription: Change or withdraw your cookie choices at any time. The same dialog opens from "Cookie settings" at the bottom of every page.

werkbund.name: Werkbund
werkbund.description: Straight edges, ink borders, and one signal red — matter-of-fact like a component kit, for readers who want a quiet interface.

lernwerkstatt.name: Lernwerkstatt
lernwerkstatt.description: Round shapes, sticker outlines, and a highly legible body font — warm and playful, for learning and beginner content.

skizzenbuch.name: Skizzenbuch
skizzenbuch.description: Warm paper, fineliner outlines, and hand-drawn button shapes — like a sketchbook page, for everything that is still in progress.

blaupause.name: Blaupause
blaupause.description: Fine lines, a millimeter grid, and blueprint blue instead of shadows — technical and precise, for reference and documentation.
